titleEn: Out of the Reeds, One Step at a Time!

pages.text: "Nia, come splash with us!" Moya called at the reeds. "I won't..." Nia tucked their long neck down inside. After the rain, the waterhole was crowded with animals.
Moya pushed through the reeds. "You like water play. Why not?" Nia's ears reddened. "I want to, but I'm so tall. Everyone looks at me." They hid deeper.
Through the reeds, Nia saw wildebeests and birds everywhere. If they went out, everyone might look up and stare. Their heart thumped. "I'll stay here..." Their neck drooped.
Moya stood beside Nia. "You're shy? That's okay. I felt that way my first time here. You don't have to come all the way out at once. One step at a time!" Nia lifted their head slightly.
"First, poke just your head above the reeds. Let only me see." Nia carefully raised their neck. Up popped their head! "Well done!" Moya beamed.
"Now just one step with me." Moya stayed close against Nia. Together, they stepped to the reeds' edge. Nobody stared! Nia began to smile. "One step at a time!"
At last, out of the reeds! Moya walked right beside Nia. "I'm here. One step at a time." Nia took a big breath and walked all the way to the water, though their feet trembled a little.
Mom looked up. "Welcome, Nia!" Birds chirped hello. Everyone did look—but everyone was smiling. Nia swayed their neck. "I came out!"
Now Nia knew what to do when shy. "One, say 'I'm shy.' Two, poke my head out first. Three, go farther one step at a time!" Next day, Nia came out first. "Moya, I'm here!"

Mom rubbed her neck against Nia's legs. "It's okay to be shy. Just take one step at a time." Moya leaned against Nia's side. Little steps had brought them to the water. Out of the reeds, one step at a time!
